tier_reason: The NEWS file (2018-11-18 release section) states paste/paste0 are about two to six times faster than in R-3.4.0, a first-party statement with no benchmark script, compiler, flags or CPU model; the author's 2018 blog timings against R-3.5.1 (seen as WebSearch snippets only, blog blocked) are also first-party, so tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: NEWS (release 2018-11-18): paste and paste0 are 'about two to six times faster than in R-3.4.0, and are usually faster than the stri_paste function from the stringi package'. Other GNU R comparisons in NEWS: the rewritten parser (release 2015-09-14) is 'usually about a factor of 1.5 faster than the parser in R-3.2.2' and sometimes enormously faster; rep and rep.int (release 2014-09-30) are 'often substantially faster in pqR than in R-2.15.2 or later R Core versions to at least R-3.1.1'. The 'up to a factor two or more' gain for replacing parts of vectors or lists with [ ], [[ ]] and $ is from the 2016-10-05 release and is relative to the previous pqR release, not to GNU R.
corrections.caveats: Claims are release-note statements without a benchmark script, hardware or compiler flags; the main baseline (R-3.4.0, 2017) is old and modern GNU R 4.x with the byte compiler/JIT may have closed some gaps. The record's vector/list replacement speedup was measured against an earlier pqR, not GNU R. The author's blog post 'New version of pqR, with major speed improvements' (2018-11-25) reports, per WebSearch snippets only (blog, r-bloggers and pqR-project.org are blocked here), a vector element replacement test taking 4.360 s in R-3.5.1 versus 0.257 s in pqR-2018-11-18 on an Intel Skylake (about 17x), another arithmetic/conditional test almost 2x faster, and a garbage-collection test at 14.129 s (R-3.5.1, JIT on) versus 8.257 s; these are first-party and their scripts were not opened. NEWS also says pqR's own matrix multiplication is generally less than a factor of two slower than optimized BLAS such as OpenBLAS (not faster). A third-party paper ('Database-Inspired Optimizations for Statistical Analysis', snippet only) found Renjin outperforming both GNU R and pqR in its scenarios. Based on R-2.15.0/2.15.1, so newer R language features and packages may be incompatible. Last commit on every branch is 2020-07-23.

notes: Real, notable alternative R interpreter by Radford Neal; tier C stays (first-party release notes and blog numbers only, no published methodology). Metadata checked on github.com: 240 stars, 16 forks, not a fork, not archived, default branch Release-2020-07-23 with last commit 2020-07-23 (no newer branch), README says GPL version 2 or version 3, so license, usability copyable and abandoned status stand. Shortcomings to record: old baseline (R-3.4.0/R-3.5.1), no benchmark scripts or hardware/compiler details in the repo, record misattributed the vector-replacement gain (it was vs earlier pqR), project abandoned since 2020 and based on R-2.15.
